best_for: PSP owners who want to replay their own games in HD on a Windows PC, Mac or Linux box, with save states and a controller.
description:
PPSSPP is a PSP emulator from the PPSSPP Project. Many people have contributed to its code, which is why more games keep working with each release.

You can carry on with a game by copying save data over from your real PSP. Rewind lets you step back a few moments after a mistake; turn it on with Rewind Snapshot Interval in the System settings. You can also turn on anisotropic filtering to improve the graphics. To try local ad hoc multiplayer, you can open a second copy of the emulator and turn on its built-in ad hoc server, though the project admits it is not perfectly smooth.

points.title: Sharper than the original
points.text: PPSSPP renders PSP games at full HD or higher, can upscale blurry textures and apply post-processing shaders. Save states let you stop and resume anywhere.

points.title: No BIOS needed
points.text: The emulator simulates the PSP's firmware, so games run without any system files. You do need your own games as .ISO or .CSO files; the project does not supply them.

points.title: Free, with an optional Gold
points.text: PPSSPP is open source under GPL 2.0 or later. PPSSPP Gold for Windows and macOS is functionally the same and exists to fund development; every price level gets the same download rights.

points.title: PSP only
points.text: It does not play PS1, PS2, Vita or other consoles' discs, and it cannot reach the PlayStation Store. Version 1.21 is set to add optional firmware for PSP-format PS1 downloads, but that is still experimental.

points.title: Controllers just work on Windows
points.text: XInput and DirectInput pads, including any Xbox 360 controller, are picked up without setup on Windows.

points.title: Installer or portable
points.text: Windows has a per-machine installer for x64 plus portable zips for x86, x64 and Arm64. macOS gets one universal .dmg. The Linux Flatpak is verified on Flathub as the developer's own, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 14 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
